contexts.text: Faith and truth are one, wherefore the ancients... instead of faith, said truth. Hence also it is that, in the Hebrew language, truth and faith are one word, which is Amuna, or amen. AR 111.
Amen = Divine confirmation from truth, thus from the Lord Himself. Amen = truth, and because the Lord was the Truth itself, He so often said, Verily I say unto you.
Even so, amen = Divine confirmation that so it would be.
Amen = Divine confirmation that it is the truth.

These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true Witness = the Lord as to the Word, which is Divine truth from Himself. Amen is Divine confirmation from the truth itself, which is the Lord, thus from the Lord.
The four Animals said amen = Divine confirmation from the Word. Amen = Divine confirmation from the truth itself, thus from the Word.
Saying amen () = Divine truth, and confirmation therefrom.

Amen () = the consent of all. In this verse, amen is said at the beginning, and now it is said at the end. When it is said at the beginning, it = truth, and confirmation therefrom; but when at the end, it = confirmation, and the consent of all that it is the truth.
Amen () = confirmation and consent from the truth.
Verily, verily = that it is the truth; and because the Lord was the Truth itself, He therefore said this so often. He himself is also called the Amen. TCR 777.

Amen = Divine confirmation. Amen = truth, for this is signified by amen in the Hebrew language; and since all truth that is truth is Divine, therefore amen = Divine confirmation; for truth confirms all things. And since the Lord was the Truth itself when He was in the world, He therefore said verily so often. AE 40.
The four Animals said amen = confirmation from the Lord out of the Inmost Heaven... Amen = confirmation from the Divine, and also the truth.

Saying amen = the Lord as to Divine truth from Divine good. Amen = the truth; and since the Lord is the Truth itself, by amen, in the highest sense, is signified the Lord as to Divine Truth. This therefore is here signified by amen, because the speech is to the Lord from the Angels of the three Heavens. Amen being here mentioned in the first place as well as in the last, signifies that the Lord as to Divine truth from Divine good is in first principles and in ultimates.

Amen = confirmation from the Divine... Amen = the truth, and hence that it is Divine truth from the Lord; but here, confirmation from the Divine, because it is the termination of the adoration of the Angels... When anyone speaks Divine truth from the heart, the Lord confirms it; confirmation can come from no other source. This is signified by amen at the end of prayer.
